description: Defending information and systems end to end: threats and malware, password attacks, applied cryptography, authentication, intrusion detection, firewalls and honeypots, ethical hacking and network attacks, and the management side of standards, audits and disaster recovery. Taught to the depth of a leading computer security course and the professional security certifications.
modelledOn: Whitman and Mattord, Principles of Information Security
Pfleeger, Pfleeger and Margulies, Security in Computing
ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, CompTIA Security+ objectives
outcomes: Explain the CIA triad and extended security properties and classify threats, vulnerabilities and controls.
Analyse how malware, backdoors and password attacks work and defend against them.
Apply cryptography and authentication mechanisms correctly in systems.
Deploy and tune intrusion detection, firewalls and honeypots and read their output.
Carry out authorised reconnaissance, scanning and exploitation in a lab and write a penetration test report.
Manage information security with policies, risk assessment, standards, audits and business continuity planning.

units.title: Information security fundamentals
topics: The CIA triad; authenticity, accountability, non-repudiation; the security versus usability trade-off
Assets, threats, vulnerabilities, risks, controls; attack surfaces and threat modelling (STRIDE)
Security principles: least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties
The security landscape in Ghana: mobile-money fraud, sakawa, ransomware against institutions, the Cyber Security Authority

units.title: Addressing threats: backdoors, viruses, worms and malware
topics: Malware taxonomy: viruses, worms, trojans, backdoors, rootkits, ransomware, spyware, botnets; famous cases (Morris worm, Stuxnet, WannaCry)
Infection vectors: phishing, drive-by downloads, removable media, supply chain; social engineering
How antivirus and endpoint detection work: signatures, heuristics, behaviour, sandboxing; evasion
Safe malware analysis in an isolated lab: static and dynamic basics
Software vulnerabilities: buffer overflows, injection, race conditions; CVE and CVSS; patch management

units.title: Password cracking and authentication
topics: Password storage: hashing, salting, slow hashes; what happens in a breach
Attacks: brute force, dictionary, rainbow tables, credential stuffing, spraying; John the Ripper and hashcat in the lab
Password policies that work; password managers; passphrases
Authentication factors; OTP, TOTP, SMS and its weaknesses, hardware keys, FIDO2/WebAuthn, biometrics
Single sign-on, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, Kerberos; session management
Access control models: DAC, MAC, RBAC, ABAC

units.title: Cryptography in practice
topics: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashes, MACs and signatures as tools
TLS, VPNs, disk and file encryption, encrypted messaging; certificates and PKI
Common misuse: ECB, hard-coded keys, weak randomness, home-made crypto
Steganography and watermarking in brief

units.title: Intrusion detection systems
topics: Host and network IDS/IPS; signature-based versus anomaly-based detection; false positives and negatives
Snort and Suricata rules; Zeek; OSSEC/Wazuh
Log management and SIEM; correlation and alerting
Deploying an IDS in the lab and detecting a scan and an exploit

units.title: Firewalls and honeypots
topics: Firewall types: packet filtering, stateful, application-layer, next-generation; architectures (DMZ, screened subnet)
Writing rules: iptables/nftables, pfSense; web application firewalls
Honeypots and honeynets: low and high interaction, deception, legal issues
Network segmentation and zero-trust architecture

units.title: Introduction to ethical hacking
topics: Legal and ethical framework: authorisation, scope, rules of engagement, Ghana's Cybersecurity Act
The penetration testing methodology: reconnaissance (OSINT), scanning (nmap), enumeration, vulnerability assessment (OpenVAS, Nessus), exploitation (Metasploit), post-exploitation, reporting
Web application testing with OWASP Top Ten: injection, broken authentication, XSS, IDOR; Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP
Wireless and social engineering assessments
Writing a penetration test report and remediation plan

units.title: Network attacks and defences
topics: Sniffing, ARP spoofing, DNS spoofing, man-in-the-middle, session hijacking
Denial of service and DDoS: SYN floods, amplification; mitigation
Wireless attacks: WEP/WPA cracking, evil twins; securing Wi-Fi
Hardening hosts and networks; secure configuration baselines (CIS Benchmarks)

units.title: Management of information security
topics: Security governance; roles (CISO), policies, standards, procedures, guidelines; security awareness training
Risk management: identification, assessment (qualitative and quantitative, ALE), treatment
Legal and regulatory: Data Protection Act 843, Cybersecurity Act 2020, PCI DSS, GDPR for international customers
Incident response planning and the incident life cycle

units.title: Security management models, standards, audits and disaster recovery
topics: Models: ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and 27002 controls, NIST CSF and SP 800-53, COBIT; the Bell-LaPadula and Biba models
Security audits and compliance; vulnerability management programmes; security metrics
Business continuity and disaster recovery: BIA, RTO/RPO, backup strategies, hot/warm/cold sites, testing the plan
Capstone: a security assessment and ISMS plan for a small organisation

schedule.title: Security principles and the threat landscape
schedule.exercise: List the assets, threats and controls for a mobile money agent kiosk and rate each risk as likely or unlikely with a reason.

tasks.title: Classify 10 incidents as breaches of confidentiality, integrity or availability and note which control would have helped
Draw a data flow diagram of a mobile money transfer and mark trust boundaries and at least six STRIDE threats
Redesign a flat office network using defence in depth and least privilege, then test that a compromised PC cannot reach the finance server

schedule.title: Malware and infection
schedule.exercise: Compare a worm, a trojan and ransomware in a table by how they spread, what they do and how you would detect them.

tasks.title: Match 12 malware descriptions to their types and read how each famous case spread, then check your answers against the rubric
Judge 10 emails and messages as phishing or genuine, mark the clues and choose a response for each in the scenario
Write a signature rule and a behaviour rule for a harmless test file in the lab VM and compare detection after the file is repacked

schedule.title: Malware analysis and vulnerabilities
schedule.exercise: Read a CVE entry and its CVSS vector, and decide how soon a clinic should patch it and why.

tasks.title: Inspect a harmless sample in the isolated lab VM with strings and file hashes, and record three observations in an analysis note
Find and fix an SQL injection flaw in a small sample web page by using parameterised queries and retest with the same attack
Prioritise a list of 10 vulnerabilities by CVSS score, exposure and asset value for a small hospital, and defend the patch order

schedule.title: Passwords and hashing
schedule.exercise: Explain why a salted slow hash protects users after a database leak, and write a password policy of five rules for a school portal.

tasks.title: Hash the same password with and without a salt in Python, show that two users with equal passwords get different salted hashes
Crack a given file of 10 unsalted hashes with a wordlist in the lab VM and report which passwords fell and how long it took
Calculate the guessing time for passwords and passphrases at a given hash rate and recommend a policy that balances strength and usability

schedule.title: Authentication and access control
schedule.exercise: Compare SMS codes with authenticator apps and hardware keys for a bank customer, and explain a SIM-swap attack.

tasks.title: Generate time-based one-time codes from a shared secret in Python and verify that a code expires after its 30 second window
Set up users, groups and file permissions in the lab VM so a clerk can read, a manager can edit and an outsider has no access
Design role-based access for a clinic system with at least five roles, test it against ten requests and fix any privilege conflicts found

schedule.title: Applied cryptography
schedule.exercise: Explain which tool you would use to keep a file private, prove who sent it and detect tampering, and why one tool is not enough.

tasks.title: Encrypt and decrypt a message with a symmetric cipher and then compute a hash, showing one changed letter alters the hash completely
Create a self-signed certificate, serve a page over TLS in the lab VM and inspect the certificate's subject, issuer and expiry date
Show that ECB mode leaks patterns in an encrypted image, then repair it with CBC or GCM and spot a hard-coded key in sample code

schedule.title: Intrusion detection and monitoring
schedule.exercise: Explain the trade-off between false positives and false negatives in an IDS, and write three Snort-style rules in plain words.

tasks.title: Place an IDS sensor on a mirrored switch port and write a rule that alerts on any ICMP echo request to the server
Run a port scan against the lab network and write a rule that detects it, then confirm the alert and the source address
Correlate web server and firewall logs in the lab VM to reconstruct an attack timeline and write a rule that alerts on its pattern

schedule.title: Firewalls, honeypots and segmentation
schedule.exercise: Draw a screened subnet for a small bank branch and list which traffic each firewall rule allows or blocks.

tasks.title: Write ACL rules on a router to allow web and DNS from the LAN to the internet and block everything else, then test with pings
Build a screened subnet with a web server in the DMZ and verify the internet can reach it but not the internal LAN
Segment a flat network into VLANs for staff, finance and guests with inter-VLAN rules, and prove guests cannot reach finance

schedule.title: Penetration testing method
schedule.exercise: Write the scope and rules of engagement for a test of a school's web portal, stating what is out of bounds.

tasks.title: Decide which of 8 testing actions are authorised under a given scope and rules of engagement and explain each ruling
Scan the lab target with nmap, enumerate its services and list three vulnerabilities with the evidence for each
Find and exploit an XSS and an IDOR flaw in the lab web app, then write the fix for each and retest

schedule.title: Wireless, social engineering and reporting
schedule.exercise: Draft the executive summary of a penetration test report for a non-technical manager, with three prioritised recommendations.

tasks.title: Respond to a pretexting phone call scenario, choose what to disclose at each step and review the feedback on your choices
Audit a simulated wireless network, find the weak encryption setting and the rogue access point and recommend fixes
Write a report from five test findings with severity ratings, evidence and remediation steps, and have it scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Network attacks and hardening
schedule.exercise: Describe how ARP spoofing enables a man-in-the-middle attack and which controls stop it.

tasks.title: Capture packets on a hub-based LAN, find an unencrypted login in the capture and explain why HTTPS would have prevented it
Flood a server with SYN packets in the simulator, observe the effect and apply a rate limit or SYN cookies to restore service
Harden a default Linux server against a benchmark checklist of 15 items, then rescan to show the number of failures reduced

schedule.title: Governance, risk and incident response
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page acceptable use policy and a short incident response checklist for a small microfinance office.

tasks.title: Compute single loss expectancy and annualised loss expectancy for five risks and rank them to choose where to spend a budget
Lead the response to a ransomware incident through the life cycle phases and be scored on containment, evidence and communication
Advise a company on a data breach notification under the local data protection law and score the choices on timing and content

schedule.title: Security frameworks, continuity and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present your ISMS plan for a small organisation, listing top risks, chosen controls, owners and review dates.

tasks.title: Calculate RTO and RPO fit for three systems against backup schedules and mark which backup strategy fails the target
Map ten security controls to the ISO 27001 and NIST CSF functions in a scenario and justify each placement
Assess a small organisation, build a risk register of at least 10 risks and write an ISMS plan scored against the rubric
